result.topic_en: Ramanujan derives formulas for Q_6(N) (related to sums of six squares) for N factored into primes, and determines the form of N giving the maximum order of Q_6(N), with an asymptotic expression for that maximum order.
result.transcription:
Add Ms a 94 18(49) (49) (93)
Let $N = 2^{a_2}.3^{a_3}.5^{a_5}\cdots\cdots p^{a_p}$,
where $a_r \ge 0$. Then from (390) we can show, as in the previous sec-
tion, that if $2^{-a_2}N$ be of the form $4n+1$, then
(393) $Q_6(N) = N^2.\frac{1-(2^2)^{-a_2-1}}{1-2^{-2}}.\frac{1-(-3^2)^{-a_3-1}}{1+3^{-2}}.\frac{1-(5^2)^{-a_5-1}}{1-5^{-2}}\cdots\cdots\frac{1-\{(-1)^{\frac{p-1}{2}}p^2\}^{-a_p-1}}{1-(-1)^{\frac{p-1}{2}}p^{-2}}$;
and if $2^{-a_2}N$ be of the form $4n-1$, then
(394) $Q_6(N) = N^2.\frac{1+(2^2)^{-a_2-1}}{1-2^{-2}}.\frac{1-(-3^2)^{-a_3-1}}{1+3^{-2}}.\frac{1-(5^2)^{-a_5-1}}{1-5^{-2}}\cdots\cdots\frac{1-\{(-1)^{\frac{p-1}{2}}p^2\}^{-a_p-1}}{1-(-1)^{\frac{p-1}{2}}p^{-2}}$,
It follows from (393) and (394) that, in order that $Q_6(N)$ should
be of maximum order, $2^{-a_2}N$ must be of the form $4n-1$ and
$a_2, a_3, a_7, a_{11}, \cdots$ must be $0$; $3, 7, 11, \ldots$ being primes of the form
$4n-1$. But all these cannot be satisfied at the same time since
$2^{-a_2}N$ cannot be of the form $4n-1$, when $a_3, a_7, a_{11}, \ldots$ are all
zeros. So let us retain a single prime of the form $4n-1$ in
the end, that is to say, the largest prime of the form $4n-1$ not
exceeding $p$. Thus we see that, in order that $Q_6(N)$ should be
of maximum order, $N$ must be of the form
$5^{a_5}.13^{a_{13}}.17^{a_{17}}\cdots\cdots p^{a_p}.p'$,
where $p$ is a prime of the form $4n+1$ and $p'$ is the prime of the
form $4n-1$ next above or below $p$; and consequently
$Q_6(N) = \frac{5}{3}N^2.\frac{1-5^{-2(a_5+1)}}{1-5^{-2}}.\frac{1-13^{-2(a_{13}+1)}}{1-13^{-2}}\cdots\cdots\frac{1-p^{-2(a_p+1)}}{1-p^{-2}}\{1-(p')^{-2}\}$.
From this we can show that the maximum order of $Q_6(N)$ is
(395) $\frac{5N^2 e^{\frac{1}{2}Li\left(\frac{1}{2\log N}\right)+O\left\{\frac{1}{\log N\log\log N\sqrt{(\log N)}}\right\}}}{3(1-\frac{1}{5^2})(1-\frac{1}{13^2})(1-\frac{1}{17^2})(1-\frac{1}{29^2})\cdots\cdots}$
$= \frac{5N^2\left\{1+\frac{1}{2}Li\left(\frac{1}{2\log N}\right)+O\frac{1}{\log N\log\log N\sqrt{(\log N)}}\right\}}{3(1-\frac{1}{5^2})(1-\frac{1}{13^2})(1-\frac{1}{17^2})(1-\frac{1}{29^2})\cdots}$
where $5, 13, 17, \ldots$ are the primes of the form $4n+1$.
